steps.label: claims_summary_gold vs. claims_detail_gold

eyebrow: The rule the next lesson's security design hangs on
code:
RULE: a table only needs row filters and column
masks if a single row can be tied back to a named,
identifiable patient.

claims_summary_gold -- clinic + day grain, no
  patient_name, no patient_ssn. Safe to query broadly.

claims_detail_gold -- one row per claim, patient_name
  and patient_ssn present. Protection has to be airtight.
caption: Aggregation itself is a form of de-identification -- that's the whole fork.

eyebrow: Gold forks into two tables, on purpose
code:
claims_summary_gold          claims_detail_gold
  clinic_id                     claim_id
  summary_date                  clinic_id
  total_billed_usd               patient_name
  claim_count                      patient_ssn
  denial_rate                       claim_amount_usd
caption: Same source data, two very different audiences -- and two very different risk profiles.

subtitle: Who sees a patient's name, and who sees NULL.
